title: Putnami first-party WebSocket wire protocol v1
description: The closed frame vocabulary of a first-party WebSocket transport. Admission happens in band, in the first client frame, on a socket opened with the putnami.service.v1 subprotocol and no handshake header; the conversation then follows the published state machine await-init, await-ready, open, half-closed, terminal.

version.description: The wire protocol version. Only version 1 exists; a peer refuses any other value instead of guessing a dialect.

token.description: A bounded opaque identifier: URL-safe characters only, so it can never smuggle a control character into a log line or a close reason.

uint64.description: Canonical decimal uint64; readers additionally reject values above 18446744073709551615. Sequences and deadlines travel as text so a JavaScript reader never loses the low bits of a value past 2^53.

positiveUint64.description: Canonical positive decimal uint64; readers additionally enforce the uint64 maximum. Message sequences start at 1.

credential.description: One resolved credential, selected by a declared profile. Credential values are first-frame material: they never appear in a URL, a subprotocol list, a diagnostic, a telemetry attribute, a close reason, or generated source.

profile.description: The name of a credential profile declared in the provider's x-putnami-client document.

value.description: The resolved credential value for that profile, bounded so a socket cannot be used to push an unbounded secret.

header.description: One ordinary request header carried in band. Authentication, client identity, tracing, hop-by-hop and WebSocket negotiation headers have dedicated fields and cannot be overridden here.

name.description: The header field name, restricted to RFC 9110 token characters and refused when it collides with a reserved or credential-carrying name.

values.description: The header's ordered values; between 1 and 32, each free of CR, LF and NUL so no value can split a frame or a log record.

context.description: Bounded propagation carried in the protected init frame rather than in the URL or the subprotocol list, which a browser exposes and a proxy logs.

traceparent.description: The W3C traceparent of the calling span, so the stream joins the caller's trace.

tracestate.description: The W3C tracestate accompanying traceparent, forwarded opaquely.

baggage.description: W3C baggage forwarded opaquely; it is bounded and never interpreted by the transport.

requestId.description: The caller's request identity, so provider logs correlate with the caller's without a header the browser cannot set.

resume.description: A request to resume a previously admitted server stream. It is legal only when the selected transport declares websocket.resume.

token.description: The resume token the provider issued on a previous ready frame. It is sensitive first-frame material.

afterSequence.description: The last sequence the caller received completely. The provider resumes strictly after it, so no delivered value repeats and none is skipped.

jsonPayload.description: A JSON-encoded application payload. The authored JSON value is preserved exactly, including numeric literals a float would round.

encoding.description: Marks the payload as JSON, matching the selected transport's declared encoding.

protoPayload.description: A protobuf-encoded application payload. The contract accepts it in v1 even where a runtime cannot yet decode it: an undeliverable transport is a strict generation error, never a runtime refusal.

encoding.description: Marks the payload as protobuf, matching the selected transport's declared encoding.

base64.description: The protobuf bytes as canonical RFC 4648 base64; readers additionally re-encode and compare, so a non-canonical spelling is refused.

payload.description: One application payload in exactly one of the two declared encodings.

init.description: The mandatory first client frame and the only admission channel. It carries the identity, credentials, budgets and propagation a browser cannot put in a handshake header.

v.description: The wire protocol version this frame is encoded in.

type.description: Identifies the frame as the admission request.

operationId.description: The generated operation being opened. The provider refuses an init that does not name the operation the upgraded route belongs to.

clientId.description: The calling client's declared identity, checked against the operation's authorized clients.

deadlineUnixMs.description: Absolute Unix epoch milliseconds, or 0 when no total deadline applies; idle and handshake bounds still apply.

budgetMs.description: Remaining total budget in milliseconds, or 0 when no total deadline applies; idle and handshake bounds still apply.

credentials.description: The resolved credentials, which must satisfy exactly one declared security alternative. The array is present even when empty.

headers.description: The declared ordinary headers for this call. The array is present even when empty.

context.description: Bounded trace and request propagation for this call.

resume.description: Present only when the caller resumes a previously admitted server stream.

request.description: The single request message of a server-streaming operation, which has no client message direction.

ready.description: Admission: the provider proves authentication and authorization completed before its handler sees any application message. It is sent exactly once.

v.description: The wire protocol version this frame is encoded in.

resumed.description: True when the provider honoured the init frame's resume request. It is always present, so a reader never infers resumption from an absent field.

resumeToken.description: The token a later call passes back in init.resume. It is required when resumed is true and may also be issued on a fresh stream.

message.description: One ordered application message. Sequences are per-direction and gap-free, so a reader detects a lost or reordered message instead of absorbing it.

v.description: The wire protocol version this frame is encoded in.

type.description: Identifies the frame as an application message.

sequence.description: The message's position in its own direction, starting at 1 or continuing after a resumed afterSequence.

payload.description: The application value, in the transport's declared encoding.

halfClose.description: Ends the client message direction while leaving the provider direction live. It is client-only: the provider terminates with result or error.

v.description: The wire protocol version this frame is encoded in.

type.description: Identifies the frame as the end of the client message direction.

result.description: The single successful terminal provider frame. On a server stream it carries no payload: values are delivered as message frames, and a payload here would be a second, undeclared delivery channel.

v.description: The wire protocol version this frame is encoded in.

type.description: Identifies the frame as successful termination.

payload.description: The final response of a client-streaming or bidirectional operation.

remoteError.description: A typed framework error. It carries framework fields only: never a raw response, headers, credential values, or an arbitrary server cause.

status.description: The HTTP status the same failure would carry over REST, so one declared error maps across transports.

code.description: The stable framework error code, in the dotted snake_case vocabulary of go/framework/errors. It is what selects the declared error a generated client raises.

grpcCode.description: The equivalent gRPC status code, present when the operation also declares a Connect transport.

retryable.description: Whether the provider states this failure may be retried, so the caller does not infer retryability from the status alone.

message.description: A bounded human-readable message. It is diagnostic text, never a machine contract.

details.description: The declared error's structured payload, matching the schema the operation declares for this code.

error.description: The single failed terminal provider frame. It is also how a refused admission is reported, so a rejection stays a decodable typed error instead of an opaque close code.

v.description: The wire protocol version this frame is encoded in.

type.description: Identifies the frame as failed termination.

error.description: The typed framework error that terminates the conversation.

cancel.description: Caller-initiated termination, without an arbitrary reason string. It is client-only and legal from init onwards: before init no operation identity exists to cancel.

v.description: The wire protocol version this frame is encoded in.

type.description: Identifies the frame as caller-initiated termination.

code.description: Why the caller stopped: an explicit cancellation or an elapsed deadline. The spelling is the framework's own, canceled.

heartbeat.description: Liveness in either direction. It is legal from await-ready onwards, so a slow admission — an asynchronous credential check — does not trip the idle budget before ready.

v.description: The wire protocol version this frame is encoded in.

type.description: Whether the frame solicits liveness or answers it.

nonce.description: The bounded token a pong echoes back, so a peer matches an answer to its own ping.

pong.description: The answer to a ping, echoing its nonce.
